title: Sexual Reproduction and Variation
seo_title: Grade 7 Natural Sciences: Sexual Reproduction and Variation Worksheets (CAPS)
standard_code: Grade 7 Natural Sciences: Sexual reproduction; variation
standard_text: Flowering plants reproduce sexually: pollination, fertilisation, seed and fruit formation and dispersal. Humans reach puberty and reproduce sexually. Offspring of sexual reproduction show variation; variation within a species helps it survive. (summary of CAPS Natural Sciences, Grade 7, Life and Living: Sexual reproduction; variation)
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 Natural Sciences worksheets (CAPS): flowers, pollination, fertilisation, seed dispersal, puberty, human reproduction and variation. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Sexual reproduction joins a male and a female sex cell.
key_sub: Offspring vary, which helps a species survive.
body_html:
How to think about it

In flowering plants, pollen (male) is carried from the anther to the stigma by insects, birds or wind (pollination). A pollen tube grows to the ovule, where fertilisation happens; the ovule becomes a seed and the ovary becomes a fruit. Seeds are dispersed by wind, water, animals or by bursting.

At puberty the body changes so that it can reproduce: girls start to menstruate and boys start to make sperm. Fertilisation happens when a sperm joins an egg. Because offspring get genes from two parents, they vary; this variation helps a species survive when conditions change.

Example

Where does pollen have to land for pollination?

The sticky top of the carpel

Answer: on the stigma

Example

Which part of a flower becomes the fruit?

It surrounds the ovules.

Answer: the ovary

Common mistakes

  • Mixing up pollination and fertilisation.
  • Thinking all fruits are sweet.
  • Thinking children look exactly like one parent.

items.q: Is natural hair colour caused by genes, by the environment, or by both?
items.e: Some features are inherited, some come from how we live, and many depend on both.

items.q: Two Labrador dogs have puppies. What will the offspring be?
c: a completely different kind of animal or plant
Labrador puppies that are similar but not identical
identical to each other in every way
items.e: Living things produce offspring of the same kind, but offspring normally vary.

items.q: Is shoe size an example of continuous or discontinuous variation?
items.e: Continuous: any value in a range (bar graph with no gaps, or histogram). Discontinuous: distinct groups.

items.q: Which characteristic is NOT inherited, so cannot be passed on to children?
